_why: The golden hash of the SHIPPED home page. Any phase not intended to change the
run must reproduce `outIndexSha256` exactly. Re-record it only after reading the
out/index.html diff by hand, and NEVER to make a red check go green.
Pinned at the tree it was measured on, per the standing rule that the number and
the sha move together. `runSourceSha256` is here so a mismatch tells you WHICH
side moved: if the source sha still matches but the output sha does not, the
build changed, not the page.
`commit` is the tree that produces `runSourceSha256`, and verify-portfolio now
asserts that pairing on every run. It has to be corrected by hand after a
re-baseline: --rebaseline writes HEAD, which is the PARENT of the commit the
new baseline lands in. This field named Phase 0 while the numbers beside it
were Phase 1's until 2026-08-06, and nothing went red because nothing looked.
The env matters. Every test:e2e:* script rebuilds with NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH=
(empty) and re-runs build-home.mjs, overwriting out/index.html. A hash taken
after one of those certifies an artifact nobody deploys. This one is taken under
the deploy configuration and verify:portfolio reproduces it in the same env,
before any e2e step runs.
Determinism was proven, not assumed: two consecutive builds at this tree produced
byte-identical output, and the result also matched an out/ built in an earlier
session. build-home.mjs and build-nameplate.mjs carry no new Date(), Date.now(),
toISOString, randomUUID or Math.random, and out/index.html carries no chunk hashes.
_closure: The hash certifies ONE file; the run's dependency closure is much larger, and
deleting a piece of it reproduces the hash byte-for-byte while breaking the live
page. These are the floors verify-portfolio.mjs asserts separately.
Sizes are floors, not equalities: a re-subset font or a retrained model should
not fail the gate, but an empty or truncated file must.
